note: recall item, found. Rs. 57′ ge-nu-wa-〈aš〉 (ending restored by the editor; TLHdig selects gen=u- 'Knie' D/L.PL over ke=nu- 'open') šanizziuš tiešḫuš šuppariyanza ešta: the god was asleep on knees in sweet sleeps. tiešḫa- here is the sleep noun (accusative of content), not 'dream'
ritual against sleeplessness: does not sleep at night (šuptari); sees bad dreams (tešḫuš, dream sense); does not sleep a sleep (tešḫan šuppariyazzi, sleep sense). Dream co-occurrence genuine; no knee
Hedammu: tešḫaš ēpta 'sleep seized him', he sleeps (šuppariyanza) like ox and ass. tešḫa- = sleep, not dream. No knee
Gilgamesh: 'we slept' (šuppariyawaštati), then Enkidu tells the dream he saw (Ù-an uḫḫun): dream via logogram only (broad count)
both verbs: 'either he sleeps (šešzi) with his wife or he sleeps (šuppariyattari)': šeš- = lie (with), šuppariya- = be asleep
both verbs: dream report; 'when I lay down (katta šeššun)' ... 'I slept again (appa šuppariyanun)' ... 'I saw'. šeššun is unannotated (???), matched by spelling

Pišaiša myth: Ištar lies down to sleep (šešuwanzi), Pišaiša lies with her (kattan šešta); later he kneels at her knees (genuwaš kattan ... ḫaliya-) in supplication. Knee co-occurrence with šeš- is real but a separate event (kneeling). genuwaš had no selection (amb), so the automatic count missed it
Instructions for temple personnel: go up to the temple to sleep (šešuwanzi); 'let there be no sleep for you' (Ù-aš / tešḫaš lē ešzi): tešḫa- = sleep (staying awake on watch)

Muršili's plague prayer: the priests shall sleep in purity (šuppa šeški(š)kanzi: šuppa = 'pure', the false-friend case) so that someone may see it in a dream (tešḫit): incubation, šeš- + dream (dream sense)
long paragraph (Muršili): šeškeškenun 'I used to sleep' (in a bed) and tešḫaniškewan 'appearing in dreams' in different sections of one long paragraph
oracle text: Ù-TUM 'dream' His Majesty saw ... 'His Majesty sleeps (šešzi) and speaks' (dream logogram; broad count)
